decomposition_parent: Formal salutation and signature block present

sibling_surface_component.name: Letter furniture: salutation and signature block
sibling_surface_component.instruction: Score only the presence of formal letter furniture. Score 10 when the comment both opens with a formal salutation ('Dear Administrator', 'Dear Sir or Madam', 'To Whom It May Concern') and closes with a signature block naming a person or organisation, typically with a complimentary close ('Sincerely,', 'Respectfully submitted,'). Score 5 when exactly one of the two is present. Score 0 when neither is present. This is a formatting judgement: score the salutation and signature block as text objects and nothing else. Do not read the body. A blank form letter with a salutation and a signature block scores 10; a detailed, expert, substantive comment that begins mid-argument and ends without a sign-off scores 0.

why_separable: A letter opening 'Dear Administrator' and closing with a typed name and title but never saying what the writer does scores 0 here and 10 on the sibling, while an unsigned first-person account from a named permit holder describing their own operation scores high here and 0 there.
criterion_name_final: Identified accountable author with stated standing
criterion_instruction_final: Score whether the text names the author or organisation and states a role, occupation, expertise, or regulated relationship to the rule's subject that lets a reader weigh its claims. Score 10 when both are present (for example, 'I have operated a licensed facility of this type for eleven years'). Score 5 when standing is asserted vaguely, naming no role, activity, or relationship. Score 0 when nothing establishes the writer's relation to the rule; salutations, signature blocks, titles, and letterhead never count.
original_instruction: Score whether the comment establishes who is speaking and what experience or position backs what it says. Score 10 when the text names the author or organisation AND states a role, occupation, expertise, or regulated relationship to the subject of the rule that a reader can use to weigh the claims (for example, 'I have operated a licensed facility of this type for eleven years', 'we are the trade association whose members hold these permits'). Score 5 when standing is asserted but left vague ('an interested professional', 'a concerned industry group') with no role, activity, or relationship named. Score 0 when nothing in the text establishes who the writer is relative to the rule, no matter how formally the letter is addressed or signed. Ignore salutations, signature blocks, titles after a name, and letterhead entirely: they are not standing.

auditor_verdict.label: incidental
auditor_verdict.justification: A comment can score 10 by merely naming an author and stating an occupation/relationship with zero evidence, analysis, or specificity about the rule -- fails the 'says nothing substantive' test despite the 'lets a reader weigh its claims' framing; it is an identity/standing fingerprint, not applied first-hand knowledge (that is covered separately in P14/P17).
